_meta.note: Figures the page uses that do not live on FRED. Every entry carries a source, a URL, a tier and an as-of date, and is mirrored in docs/THESIS.md (section 'September 2026 update'). TIER 1 = official statistics, central banks, IEA, IMF, WTO, Fed research. TIER 2 = Reuters, Bloomberg, FT, CNBC, S&P Global, Lloyd's List, Kpler, major outlets. TIER 3 is never load-bearing and does not appear here.
_meta.rule: If a figure here disagrees with a FRED series in the snapshot, the FRED series wins and this entry must be corrected.

ecb_reserve_shares.name: Gold vs US Treasuries as a share of global official reserves, end-2025
ecb_reserve_shares.note: ECB attributes the crossover mainly to valuation: gold rose about 60% in 2025 after about 30% in 2024. It also reports official Treasury custody at the New York Fed fell USD 82bn to USD 2.7tn in March 2026 as some central banks sold to defend their currencies after the war began.
ecb_reserve_shares.source: ECB, 'The international role of the euro', June 2026

fed_counterpoint.name: Why gold did not actually overtake Treasuries as the world's favourite reserve asset
fed_counterpoint.author: Colin Weiss, Federal Reserve Board
fed_counterpoint.finding: The crossover is a valuation effect driven by private ETF demand since late 2024, not central bank accumulation; by June 2026 foreign official Treasury holdings again exceeded world gold reserves excluding the US in dollar terms. Five legacy holders (US, Germany, Italy, France, IMF) own 52% of official gold and have not added since the 1970s. Foreign officials bought roughly USD 200bn of Treasuries net between 2022 and April 2026.

gold_price.note: No FRED series carries the LBMA price after 2022, so this is Tier 2. Gold is DOWN about a fifth from its January record; the custody story is about where gold sits, not what it costs.

dallas_fed_wp2624.title: The Incidence of Fuel-Price Shocks and Tax Holidays: Evidence from the 2026 Oil Shock
dallas_fed_wp2624.finding: The 2026 Iran war raised gasoline expenditure shares 2.9 times more in the lowest-income census tracts than in the highest; pre-shock exposure explains 89% of the gap.

dallas_fed_0417.title: Implications of the Iran war for U.S. inflation
dallas_fed_0417.finding: Current scenario: headline PCE +0.6pp and core +0.2pp Q4/Q4 2026; a three-quarter closure lifts headline by 1.1pp. Long-run expectations effect 'negligible'.
